subject: Predict problem, Error: ncol(coefficients) == length(obj@estimates) is not TRUE

messages.author: f20e19f0f77c5e8e
messages.subject: Predict problem, Error: ncol(coefficients) == length(obj@estimates) is not TRUE
parts:
Hello all,

Im trying to use predict to estimate densities to a large number of sites but it keeps giving me this error: Error: ncol(coefficients) == length(obj@estimates) is not TRUE.  This only happens when I include year as an additive effect in the model.  If I exclude year it runs fine.  The funny thing is that I have used year in another similar analysis and had no problem getting it to work by setting year at the average value.  Any ideas?

Here is my sample code:

a<-read.csv("C:/Users/Bryan/Desktop/CREP dissertation/ch.1-Multiscale models of shrubland birds/N-mixture data/gdistSampWIFLallyears.csv")
y <- a[,2:16]
db<-c(0,20,40,60,80,100)
T=3
year <- scale(a["Year"])
crop200<-scale(a["CROP_200"])
grass200<-scale(a["GRASS_200"])
for200<-scale(a["FOR_200"])
crp200<-scale(a["crp_200"])



site.Covs <- data.frame(year, crop200, grass200,for200, crp200)
site.Covs$Year <- as.factor(site.Covs$Year)

wiflumf<-unmarkedFrameGDS(y=y, siteCovs=site.Covs, survey="point", dist.breaks=db,unitsIn="m", numPrimary=T)
summary(wiflumf)


#Best Model
WIFLforestgrass<-gdistsamp(~Year+for200+grass200, ~1, ~Year, wiflumf,keyfun="halfnorm", output="density", unitsOut="ha", mixture="NB", K=50)


#Current Population Estimate
data <- read.csv("C:/Users/Bryan/Desktop/CREP dissertation/ch.2CREPPopulationestimate/N-mixture data/FedCREP_updated2010abuffer200m_1.csv",header=TRUE)

# create new data frame for prediction
newdat <- data.frame(Year=0,forest=data["for200"],grass=data["grass200"],ha=data["ha"])

# predict density for newdat using top model
mod.pred <- predict(WIFLforestgrass,newdata=newdat,type="lambda", appendData=TRUE)
popsize<-(mod.pred[,1]*(ha))
Pop<-sum(popsize[,1])

parts: Hi Bryan, why are you turning "year" into a factor after scaling it?  That is the source of your error here.
